title: Quarterly roadmap: Dedicated pool elasticity & predictive autoscale runway
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Quarter plan to deliver an adaptive dedicated-pool elasticity playbook and a predictive autoscale runway. Goal: reduce customer token tail-latency during bursts, lower committed capacity overhang by 12% through predictive hedging, and provide Ops with deterministic canary windows for capacity rollouts. Workstreams: forecasting model improvements (demand signal + calendar-aware), autoscale policy templates (guardrails for latency SLOs), contract/reservation UX changes (flex windows + two-way refunds), and SLO observability (live fill-rate + waste dashboards). This ticket coordinates cross-team milestones and defines OKRs, release criteria, and rollout staging for Q2.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscale policy library shipping with 3 templates: low-latency, cost-optimized, balanced
Forecast model integrated into capacity planner with >=10% improvement in 7-day prediction MAPE vs baseline
Canary rollout procedure documented and validated in staging with rollback automation
Console exposes per-pool 'predicted fill' and 'waste delta' charts and an alert when predicted overflow > 15%
Runbook for customer support and account teams published and linked from the console
milestones: M2: Autoscale policy spec + safety guardrails (2025-03-21)
M4: Staging canary & rollback automation test (2025-04-07)
metrics: Burst tail-latency P95 during 99th percentile traffic events
Autoscale policy adoption rate by customers
Support tickets related to capacity & billing after rollout
risks: Overfitting forecast to historical seasonality leading to missed anomalies
Autoscale policy complexity causing customer misconfiguration
Console dashboard performance regressions when querying high-cardinality pools
Contract changes may increase sales friction without clear billing UI
